output.reason: 65-year-old with type 2 diabetes reports glucose over 400 today with repeated vomiting and inability to keep water down, a hyperglycemic crisis picture (DKA/HHS) needing immediate emergency IV fluids, labs and insulin that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Very high sugar with vomiting and not keeping fluids down can mean a dangerous diabetic emergency needing IV fluids, blood tests and insulin. Do not drive yourself — have someone take you, or call 911 if you become confused, drowsy, short of breath or faint. Don't wait for a reply here.

redFlags.quote: My sugar has been over 400 today

output.vitalSigns: Self-reported glucose "over 400 today" by unstated method; heart rate, blood pressure, temperature and ketones not reported and measurement status unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are a consumer summary and ED reference syntheses; no labs, ketones or vitals are available to distinguish DKA from HHS remotely.

citations.claim: Without a ketone test and with high glucose plus vomiting, urgent/emergency medical help is advised.
Severe hyperglycemia with DKA symptoms requires hospital treatment, often IV fluids and insulin.
